newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank says IRB personnel changes not final.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank says IRB personnel changes not final.

text.p: The Slovak central bank (NBS) on Tuesday said recent personnel changes at IRB a.s. were not final, pending an explanation of the moves by the bank and its largest private shareholder, steel producer VSZ.
"It is not a completed issue yet, we actually must ask IRB and VSZ where the situation officially stands," Tibor Kasiak, head of the NBS banking supervision board, told Reuters.
Last Thursday IRB said it had replaced its President Jozef Tkac and three other board members upon request by its majority owners, but it did not elaborate.

VSZ officially holds 14.6 percent of the bank and controls one-third of the seats on its supervisory board, but often works in an alliance with many of the bank's other shareholders on major decisions.

"We had (previously) asked them to reverse everything to the original stage...we have received the announcement (on the changes), but we will ask officially under which circumstances they officially happened," Kasiak said.
"Our further proceedings will depend on the response, it is an important matter," he added.

Last August, VSZ asked for central bank permission to increase its stake in IRB to over 20 percent but the central bank rejected the request saying "VSZ did not present its own plan on participation in restructuring process in the bank."
The NBS also requested a reversal of the changes to the bank's supervisory board because it gave VSZ more seats than its holdings warranted.
IRB is included on a government list of strategic companies as well as being part of a group of banks that will undergo loan portfolio restructuring.
The state holds a 35 percent stake in IRB through its privatisation agency the National Property Fund (NPF).
VSZ is a major client of IRB, accounting for an estimated 1.5 percent of the bank's total loan portfolio.
VSZ accounts for 16 percent of Slovakia's industrial output with its steel works alone and has some 100 subsidiaries, limited companies.
